To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the decreases of pyridoxalphosphate and glutamate decarbosylase activity produced in whole mouse brain by pyridoxal‐gamma‐glutamyle hydrazone are actually produced at nerve endings.
the decreases in PLP levels and in GAD activity in brain, induced by PLPGH, actually occur in synaptosomes, the latter being the site of GABA synthesis.

the subcellular distribution pattern of PLP in brain is different from that of GAD activity, and that the inhibition of GAD by the convulsant drug PLPGH is more pronounced in the fractions in which PLP is decreased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between PLP and GAD in brain subcellular fractions, and with the effects of a drug that produces convulsions and decreases PLP levels and GAD activity in whole brain.
the localization of the PLP and GAD systems in the synaptosome, and their relationship to convulsions.
the localization of PLP in subcellular particles from mouse brain and its relationship to the activity of GABA‐synthesizing enzyme (GAD) in the same particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PLPGH produces a specific inhibition of GAD at the synaptosomes of mouse brain, and that this inhibition is associated with a decrease of PLP levels in this fraction.
the decrease of PLP levels and the inhibition of GAD produced by PLPGH are mainly restricted to the synaptoplasic compartment.
the decrease of PLP levels and GAD activity in brain, as well the convulsions induced by PLPGH, are due to a decrease of the GABA synthesis at nerve endings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PLPGH‐induced convulsions are accompanied by changes in the subcellu‐lar distribution of PLP, and these are reflected in the activity of GABA synthesizing enzymes.

PLPGH decreases the levels of PLPG in the synaptoplasms of mouse cerebral cortex, and that this decrease of PLPG in nerve endings results in a decreased activity of GABA synthesis, which in turn leads to a decreased inhibition of nerve cells and to a convulsant state.
PLPGH decreases the levels of PLPGH in the synaptoplasma and, as a consequence, the activity of GABA synthesis, which is inhibited in the nerve endings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PLP is an important factor in the regulation of the excitatory/inhibitory balance at the nerve endings.
